chunks: And from him (Al-Hilli) from Isma'il ibn Sahl from Hammad from Hariz from Al-Fudayl from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

I asked him, 'For whom is the Fitrah (Zakat al-Fitr) permissible?' He said, 'For one who does not find (the means to pay it). And that which is permissible for him is not obligatory upon him, and that which is obligatory upon him is not permissible for him.'

key_terms.الْفِطْرَة: Zakat al-Fitr (alms of breaking the fast)

ai.seo_question: Who is eligible to receive or be exempt from Zakat al-Fitr according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) clarifies the reciprocal nature of Zakat al-Fitr, establishing that exemption from obligation implies permissibility for the recipient, while obligation implies exclusivity for the payer. This ruling underscores the principle that Fitrah serves as a purifying charity for the needy, ensuring that those who are financially capable do not compete with those who are exempt. The statement highlights the precise legal boundaries of eligibility, reinforcing the social welfare aspect of the ritual in Shia jurisprudence.
